You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Design a geometric model consisting of two square plates, each with an edge length of 140mm and a thickness of 10mm. Position these plates so that they intersect at a 90-degree angle, creating an L-shape configuration. On one of these plates, incorporate a square cutout measuring 45x45mm. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept (no execution yet)

1. Decide a common reference point.  
   • Use the global origin (0 ,0 ,0) as the corner where both plates meet and where their thicknesses overlap.  
   • All dimensions are expressed in millimetres.

2. Build the first (horizontal) plate.  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z-thickness).  
   • Base-corner: (0 ,0 ,0).  
   • This is the very first solid, therefore subtraction = False.

3. Add the second (vertical) plate so it is orthogonal to the first.  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 10 mm (Y-thickness) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base-corner: (0 ,0 ,0) – it shares the same edge and thickness volume 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 and 0 ≤ Z ≤ 10 with the first plate, creating a perfect 90° L-joint.  
   • subtraction = False (it is added to the model).

4. Provide the square cut-out (45 mm × 45 mm) through one plate.  
   • Place it in the horizontal plate, centred to avoid touching the vertical plate.  
     – Centre of plate = (70 ,70).  
     – Half cut-out size = 22.5 mm.  
     – Base-corner of cut-out: (70-22.5 , 70-22.5 , 0) = (47.5 , 47.5 , 0).  
   • Extents: 45 mm (X) × 45 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z-through the full thickness).  
   • subtraction = True so this volume is removed.

5. Translate the three solids above into one block() call by supplying parallel arrays:  
   • x_size  = [140, 140,  45]  
   • y_size  = [140,  10,  45]  
   • z_size  = [ 10, 140, 10]  
   • x       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   • y       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   • z       = [  0,   0,   0]  
   • subtraction = [False, False, True]

6. After the future block() call, finish the model with finished(allFunctionsCalled=True).

When you want me to prepare the exact JSON-style block() and finished() function calls, just let me know.
